target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures focus on the benefits of edge computing/device processing, specifically noting proximity to data, reduced response time, and improved privacy, security, and personalization.

Both disclosures describe mobile devices (handsets/PCs in 2024, mobile in 2023) becoming pervasive AI platforms where complex large generative AI algorithms run on-device to enable on-demand and contextual use cases.

Both disclosures outline the vision of generative AI becoming ubiquitous and expanding beyond smartphones into other industries such as IoT, XR, and automotive.

Both disclosures address the broader trend of generative AI capabilities in edge devices, with 2023 discussing the general vision of AI expansion and 2024 providing specific adoption forecasts for generative AI capable smartphones.

The company expects generative AI to become ubiquitous, expanding beyond smartphones into industries such as compute, IoT, XR, and automotive.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
The 2024 disclosures D008 and D009 jointly describe the trend of edge AI, focusing on context-aware processing benefits (privacy, security, personalization) and the emergence of mobile handsets/PCs as pervasive AI platforms with on-device generative AI. The 2025 disclosure D008 covers the same core trend, explicitly linking processor advancements to cloud/edge distribution, restating the benefits of edge computing (privacy, security, personalization), and describing smartphones/PCs as pervasive AI platforms with on-device generative AI. The 2025 text adds details about new personal AI devices (smart glasses, earbuds), but the primary subject of on-device AI trends and device platforms matches the combined 2024 input.

The 2024 disclosure envisions generative AI becoming ubiquitous, expanding into IoT, XR, and automotive. The 2025 disclosure (qcom_2025_1_D008) contains the nearly identical sentence: 'Building on the smartphone and PC foundation, we envision AI becoming ubiquitous... as it continues to expand into industries and applications such as industrial IoT, XR and automotive.' This is a direct topical match on the specific expansion vision.

comparisons.peer_topic: Hyperscale Customer Base and Product Applications
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's data center products, including server CPUs, GPU accelerators, and adaptive SOCs, are purchased by large public cloud providers and hyperscale private data centers. These customers incorporate the products into servers for web applications, public cloud services, and AI workloads such as generative AI models.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and AMD discuss the integration of AI into computing devices, but they focus on different segments of the market. Qualcomm emphasizes the shift of large generative AI algorithms running on edge devices like mobile handsets and PCs to reduce energy costs, as stated in the target disclosure: 'With increased processing power, mobile handsets and PCs are becoming pervasive AI platforms, with complex large generative AI algorithms running on-device, enabling on-demand and contextual AI use cases at a fraction of the energy required by cloud-based applications.' In contrast, AMD focuses on how its data center products, including GPU accelerators, are purchased by hyperscale cloud providers to support public cloud AI workloads and generative AI models: 'Hyperscale data centers use these products to operate web-based applications or to support public cloud computing and storage service offerings, including but not limited to AI workloads such as generative AI models.' While both cite generative AI as a key driver, Qualcomm highlights on-device efficiency and edge processing, whereas AMD highlights cloud-scale infrastructure.

sentences.text: With increased processing power, mobile handsets and PCs are becoming pervasive AI platforms, with complex large generative AI algorithms running on-device, enabling on-demand and contextual AI use cases at a fraction of the energy required by cloud-based applications.

Hyperscale data centers use these products to operate web-based applications or to support public cloud computing and storage service offerings, including but not limited to AI workloads such as generative AI models.

comparisons.peer_summary: This solution enables organizations to use generative AI technologies while addressing privacy and compliance needs.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and Broadcom (AVGO) highlight privacy and security as advantages or requirements of on-premises or on-device AI. Qualcomm notes that edge devices enable use cases by 'intelligently processing and sharing data with cloud-based applications as needed,' implying local processing benefits. Broadcom's 'Private AI' solution explicitly 'enables organizations to use generative AI technologies while addressing privacy and compliance needs.' While Qualcomm frames local processing as a method for efficiency and contextual use, Broadcom frames private/on-device approaches specifically around mitigating privacy risks associated with generative AI, representing a shared concern for data security in AI deployment.

sentences.text: As wireless connectivity complements on-device generative AI, edge devices enable enhanced productivity use cases, while intelligently processing and sharing data with cloud-based applications as needed.
• Private AI: This solution enables organizations to use generative AI technologies while addressing privacy and compliance needs of the organization.

comparisons.peer_summary: Tanzu Data provides a suite of data services with advanced analytical data warehouse capabilities, real-time transactions, and an in-memory data grid with vector database capabilities for AI use cases.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures mention vector database capabilities or similar data structures in the context of AI, though in different contexts. Broadcom's Tanzu Data provides an 'in-memory data grid with vector database capabilities for AI use cases.' Qualcomm's disclosure does not explicitly mention vector databases but describes 'contextual AI use cases' enabled by on-device processing. While Broadcom focuses on the data infrastructure layer for AI applications, Qualcomm focuses on the end-device platform layer. The connection is weak but exists in the broad theme of AI-enabling infrastructure, specifically around data handling for AI.

sentences.text: With increased processing power, mobile handsets and PCs are becoming pervasive AI platforms, with complex large generative AI algorithms running on-device, enabling on-demand and contextual AI use cases at a fraction of the energy required by cloud-based applications.

• Tanzu Data: A suite of data services that provides advanced analytical data warehouse capabilities and real-time transactions and processing at massive scale with an in-memory data grid with vector database capabilities for AI use cases.

comparisons.peer_summary: Intel views AI as a generational shift and aims to bring AI to where data is generated and used, addressing the full AI continuum from GenAI to AI PCs and edge computing. The company leverages a spectrum of hardware and software platforms for open, modular solutions and is infusing AI into its technologies to support current and future workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and Intel explicitly identify 'AI PC' or 'PCs' as a key emerging usage area for AI technology. Qualcomm states 'mobile handsets and PCs are becoming pervasive AI platforms,' while Intel aims to address 'emerging usages like AI PCs and AI at the edge.' Both companies view the PC as a primary vehicle for bringing AI capabilities to the user. Intel further notes it is 'infusing AI into Intel technologies... fueling emerging usages like AI PC,' aligning with Qualcomm's observation of PCs becoming 'pervasive AI platforms.'

sentences.text: With increased processing power, mobile handsets and PCs are becoming pervasive AI platforms, with complex large generative AI algorithms running on-device, enabling on-demand and contextual AI use cases at a fraction of the energy required by cloud-based applications.
We also seek to address every phase of the AI continuum, from the largest, most challenging GenAI and large language models to emerging usages like AI PCs and AI at the edge.

We are infusing AI into Intel technologies, supporting today's GenAI workloads, fueling emerging usages like AI PC and AI at the edge, and pioneering innovations that we believe will help advance the future of AI in the next decade.

comparisons.peer_topic: Software strategy and open source contributions
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel aims to optimize AI frameworks and maintains the OpenVINO toolkit for deep learning inference. In 2024, Intel launched the Open Platform for Enterprise AI under the Linux Foundation and contributed oneAPI specifications to the UXL Foundation to enable open, multi-vendor programming across accelerators.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and Intel discuss software and toolkit strategies supporting on-device or edge AI inference. Qualcomm highlights the role of wireless connectivity complementing 'on-device generative AI' for 'enhanced productivity use cases.' Intel describes its software strategy, including the 'OpenVINO toolkit' which 'accelerates deep learning inference on our processors across various use cases, such as generative AI,' noting it is 'used in domains from edge to AI PC to cloud.' Both acknowledge the importance of software tools and connectivity/frameworks in enabling effective on-device or edge AI execution, though Qualcomm emphasizes the edge-cloud interaction while Intel emphasizes the open-source toolkit ecosystem.

sentences.text: As wireless connectivity complements on-device generative AI, edge devices enable enhanced productivity use cases, while intelligently processing and sharing data with cloud-based applications as needed.

Our OpenVINO™ toolkit is an open source toolkit that accelerates deep learning inference on our processors across various use cases, such as generative AI, computer vision, audio, and language with industry standard models.
It is used in domains from edge to AI PC to cloud and is the leading inferencing library on our silicon.

comparisons.peer_topic: Demand drivers for mobile memory and storage
comparisons.peer_summary: Proliferation of smartphones and tablets increases demand for high-performance memory, with on-device AI capabilities driving needs for increased memory and storage capacity.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and Micron identify on-device AI capabilities on smartphones and PCs as key growth drivers that necessitate specific hardware characteristics. Qualcomm notes that 'complex large generative AI algorithms [are] running on-device,' while Micron explicitly links the proliferation of these devices and their AI capabilities to increased demand for memory: 'Smartphones offer tremendous potential for personalized AI capabilities that offer greater security and responsiveness when executed on the device. Enabling these on-device AI capabilities is driving increased memory and storage capacity needs.' Both disclosures frame the mobile device as an 'AI platform' or device with on-device AI potential, driving product evolution, although Qualcomm focuses on the processing platform aspect and Micron on the memory/storage component requirement.

sentences.text: With increased processing power, mobile handsets and PCs are becoming pervasive AI platforms, with complex large generative AI algorithms running on-device, enabling on-demand and contextual AI use cases at a fraction of the energy required by cloud-based applications.

As wireless connectivity complements on-device generative AI, edge devices enable enhanced productivity use cases, while intelligently processing and sharing data with cloud-based applications as needed.
Smartphones offer tremendous potential for personalized AI capabilities that offer greater security and responsiveness when executed on the device.
Enabling these on-device AI capabilities is driving increased memory and storage capacity needs and increasing demand for new value-add solutions.

comparisons.peer_topic: PC market and AI-driven DRAM demand
comparisons.peer_summary: Next-generation PCs feature AI capabilities and high-performance neural processing chipsets, leading to significantly higher DRAM content, with the company announcing low-power compression-attached memory modules to support AI workloads on PCs.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures discuss the emergence of AI-capable PCs as a distinct market segment. Qualcomm states that 'mobile handsets and PCs are becoming pervasive AI platforms,' while Micron details that 'next generation PCs... contain high-performance neural processing chipsets as well as AI' and will have 'significantly more DRAM content.' Both identify AI integration in PCs as a significant market trend, with Qualcomm focusing on the platform's role in running on-device algorithms and Micron focusing on the resulting demand for higher-performance memory components to support those AI workloads.

sentences.text: With increased processing power, mobile handsets and PCs are becoming pervasive AI platforms, with complex large generative AI algorithms running on-device, enabling on-demand and contextual AI use cases at a fraction of the energy required by cloud-based applications.
The next generation PCs that have been announced contain high-performance neural processing chipsets as well as AI.
We expect these devices will have significantly more DRAM content than today's average PC.

comparisons.peer_summary: Originally used for simulating human imagination in gaming and films, GPUs now simulate human intelligence to enable deep learning, self-driving cars, and generative AI. Their parallel processing capabilities allow software to learn from large datasets, enabling enterprises to create difficult-to-build services like recommendation systems and generative content.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and NVIDIA describe the evolution of hardware to support advanced AI workloads, including generative AI. Qualcomm focuses on the deployment of these algorithms on edge devices (handsets/PCs) for efficiency: 'complex large generative AI algorithms running on-device... at a fraction of the energy required by cloud-based applications.' NVIDIA focuses on the underlying parallel processing capabilities of GPUs that enable deep learning and generative AI generally: 'Its parallel processing capabilities... are essential for deep learning algorithms... GPU-powered AI solutions are being developed... to deliver services... Examples include generative AI.' While both mention generative AI, Qualcomm's context is specifically on-device deployment and energy efficiency, whereas NVIDIA's context is broader, focusing on the GPU's fundamental role in enabling deep learning and generative AI capabilities across various applications, often implied to be larger scale or training-focused given the 'thousands of computing cores' reference.

sentences.text: With increased processing power, mobile handsets and PCs are becoming pervasive AI platforms, with complex large generative AI algorithms running on-device, enabling on-demand and contextual AI use cases at a fraction of the energy required by cloud-based applications.
Its parallel processing capabilities, supported by thousands of computing cores, are essential for deep learning algorithms.
GPU-powered AI solutions are being developed by thousands of enterprises to deliver services and products that would have been immensely difficult or even impossible with traditional coding.

Examples include generative AI, which can create new content such as text, code, images, audio, video, and molecule structures, and recommendation systems, which can recommend highly relevant content such as products, services, media or ads using deep neural networks trained on vast datasets that capture the user preferences.
